entries.summary: Both Greta hands start with 1 to 7 in one suit. Their Wind and Dragon tiles differ.
entries.whatItIs: Both hands use 1 to 7 in one suit. Greta’s Dragon adds all four Winds and a Dragon Pung or Kong. Greta’s Garden adds all four Winds and all three Dragons as singles.
entries.whatItMeans: The 1-7 run is the common visual cue. Greta's Dragon adds all four Winds and a Dragon Pung/Kong; Greta's Garden instead adds all four Winds and all three Dragons as single honours.
entries.whySpecial: The same 1 to 7 run leads to two hands with different Wind and Dragon tiles.

variants.label: Greta's Dragon
variants.definition: A 1-7 run in one suit, all four Winds and a Dragon Pung/Kong.

variants.label: Greta's Garden
variants.definition: A 1-7 run in one suit plus all four Winds and all three Dragons.

evidenceBindings.locator: §3 Runs inventory — Greta's Dragon pp.13,38; Greta's Garden pp.13,38

entries.summary: A 1-9 run in one suit, one of each Dragon and a Wind pair.
entries.whatItIs: Use 1 to 9 in one suit, one of each Dragon and a pair of Winds. The 1-9 run is nine single tiles, not Chows.
entries.whatItMeans: The nine suited tiles are singles forming 1 through 9; the remaining five tiles are the three Dragons plus two identical Winds.
entries.whySpecial: It combines a full suited run with all three Dragons and a Wind pair.

evidenceBindings.locator: §3 Dragons/honours inventory — Dragon's Run (not illustrated)

entries.summary: Two complementary suit blocks: 11, 234, 55 in one suit and 55, 678, 99 in the other.
entries.whatItIs: A fixed two-suit layout combining pairs and three-tile runs in a mirrored pattern.
entries.whatItMeans: One suit supplies the low pair/run pattern; the other supplies the high run/pair pattern, with a 5 pair present in both suits.
entries.whySpecial: The hand must use this exact two-suit arrangement.

evidenceBindings.locator: §3 Runs inventory — Yin Yang pp.14,50

entries.summary: One Chow in each suit, plus a suited Pung/Kong and suited pair.
entries.whatItIs: Make one Chow in each suit, then add a suited Pung or Kong and a suited pair. Do not use an honour set or pair.
entries.whatItMeans: The three Chows guarantee all three suits appear; the remaining Pung/Kong and pair must also be suited rather than honours.
entries.whySpecial: It uses a Chow in all three suits and no honour set or pair.

evidenceBindings.locator: §3 Runs/Chows inventory — Little Robert p.16

entries.summary: Four Circle Chows and a Circle pair, including 123, 456 and 789.

entries.whatItMeans: Three of the Chows establish 123, 456 and 789; a fourth Circle Chow and Circle pair complete the ordinary hand.
entries.whySpecial: The four Chows include the full 1-9 run in Circles.

evidenceBindings.locator: §3 Runs/Chows inventory — Moon at Bottom of Well pp.15,47,60

entries.summary: All three hands use one Chow in each suit and all four Winds, with one Wind paired. Two hands fix the Chow ranks to 1-2-3 or 7-8-9.
entries.whatItIs: Windy Chow allows any Chows. Chop Suey uses 1-2-3 in every suit. Chow Mein uses 7-8-9 in every suit.
entries.whatItMeans: Windy Chow leaves the three Chows open; Chop Suey fixes all three to 123; Chow Mein fixes all three to 789.
entries.whySpecial: The fixed Chow ranks distinguish Chop Suey and Chow Mein from Windy Chow.

entries.summary: All four Winds, all three Dragons with one Dragon paired, and three non-terminal pairs in one suit.

entries.whatItMeans: The Winds remain four singles; the Dragons contribute one pair and two singles; the remaining six tiles are three non-terminal pairs in one suit.
entries.whySpecial: All seven honour tiles appear, and three pairs complete the suited part.

evidenceBindings.locator: §3 Pairs/Winds inventory — Dragonette pp.24,39

entries.summary: Three Western hands have “Gates” in the name, but their tile patterns are different.
entries.whatItIs: Compare Confused Gates, Golden Gates and Dragon’s Gates to tell the names apart.
entries.whatItMeans: This topic exists to help a learner distinguish names, not to assert a common canonical hand. Confused Gates uses a 2-8 run plus terminal Pungs; Golden Gates uses even-rank pairs plus a terminal and corresponding Dragon; Dragon's Gates combines a 2-8 run/pair with a terminal meld and corresponding Dragon meld.
entries.whySpecial: The similar names can easily cause lookup mistakes.

variants.label: Confused Gates
variants.definition: A 2-8 run with one duplicated run tile, plus 111 and 999 in the other two suits.

variants.label: Golden Gates
variants.definition: Pairs of 2,4,6,8 in one suit plus its qualifying terminal and corresponding Dragon melds.

variants.label: Dragon's Gates
variants.definition: A 2-8 run with pair plus a same-suit terminal meld and corresponding Dragon meld.

entries.referenceNote: These hands are different from Gates of Heaven.

evidenceBindings.locator: §3 inventory — Confused Gates pp.9,51; Golden Gates pp.25,34; Dragon's Gates pp.12,34

entries.summary: Take 1 to 9 in one suit as single tiles, then add five different Winds or Dragons.
entries.whatItIs: An irregular hand joining a complete one-suit straight to five distinct honour tiles.
entries.whatItMeans: The suited nine tiles form 1 through 9 as singles; the remaining five tiles are distinct Winds/Dragons rather than pairs or melds.
entries.whySpecial: It combines a complete suited straight with five different honour tiles.

evidenceBindings.locator: §3 Runs inventory — Five Odd Honours pp.11,38

entries.summary: One suit, four sets and a pair. Western — T&M allows at most one Chow.
entries.whatItIs: A one-suit Western scoring pattern, not a fixed-value special hand.
entries.whatItMeans: The hand uses the usual four sets and a pair. One set may be a Chow.
entries.whySpecial: The same name “Purity” has a different structure under these rules.
entries.referenceNote: The score and exposure value are calculated under Western — T&M. One Chow is allowed; an exposed Chow does not count.

entries.summary: Two mirrored three-suit Pung/Kong hands with different honour anchors.
entries.whatItIs: Both hands use one non-terminal Pung or Kong in each suit. Sunrise adds an East Wind Pung or Kong and a White Dragon pair. Sunset adds a White Dragon Pung or Kong and a Red Dragon pair.
entries.whatItMeans: Sunrise uses East Wind as the meld and White Dragon as the pair; Sunset uses White Dragon as the meld and Red Dragon as the pair.
entries.whySpecial: The suited sets match, while the Wind and Dragon tiles tell the hands apart.

variants.label: Sunrise
variants.definition: East Wind Pung/Kong, White Dragon pair, and one non-terminal Pung/Kong in each suit.

variants.label: Sunset
variants.definition: White Dragon Pung/Kong, Red Dragon pair, and one non-terminal Pung/Kong in each suit.

evidenceBindings.locator: Pass 4I — Sunrise p.42/p.59; Sunset p.42/p.59

entries.summary: Four Pungs or Kongs and a pair using honours and, if used, 1s or 9s from one suit.
entries.whatItIs: Use only Winds, Dragons, and 1s or 9s from at most one numbered suit.
entries.whatItMeans: The hand uses Pungs or Kongs. Any suited tiles must all come from one suit and be 1s or 9s.
entries.whySpecial: Any suited tiles must be 1s or 9s, and they must all come from one suit.
entries.referenceNote: The score and exposure value are calculated under these rules.

evidenceBindings.locator: Pass 4I — All Honour Hand p.44/p.58

entries.summary: One suit with optional honours, mostly Pungs or Kongs, plus a pair. One Chow may be allowed.
entries.whatItIs: A named Western scoring pattern for a mostly Pung or Kong hand using one numbered suit plus optional Winds or Dragons.
entries.whatItMeans: One Chow may be used, but the rest of the hand is built from Pungs or Kongs and a pair.
entries.whySpecial: This named hand has its own rules for sets, honours and exposure.
entries.referenceNote: The score and exposure eligibility are calculated under these rules. An exposed Chow does not count.

evidenceBindings.locator: Pass 4I — Ordinary Mah Jong p.42/p.59

entries.summary: Three hands share a 1-9 run in one suit. Their honour Pung or Kong and pair tell them apart.
entries.whatItIs: Guardian Winds uses a Wind set and Wind pair. Guardian Dragons uses a Dragon set and Dragon pair. Dragon’s Tail mixes the two honour types.
entries.whatItMeans: Guardian Winds uses a Wind meld and Wind pair; Guardian Dragons uses a Dragon meld and Dragon pair; Dragon's Tail deliberately mixes the honour families, one as the meld and the other as the pair.
entries.whySpecial: The same suited run supports three hands with different honour rules.

variants.label: Guardian Winds
variants.definition: A 1-9 run, Wind Pung/Kong and Wind pair.

variants.label: Guardian Dragons
variants.definition: A 1-9 run, Dragon Pung/Kong and Dragon pair.

variants.label: Dragon's Tail
variants.definition: A 1-9 run with a Wind Pung/Kong and Dragon pair, or a Dragon Pung/Kong and Wind pair.

evidenceBindings.locator: §3 Runs inventory — Guardian Winds pp.10,39; Guardian Dragons pp.10/11,39; Dragon's Tail pp.12,41

entries.summary: Seven pairs using Green Dragons and the permitted green Bamboo tiles.
entries.whatItIs: A Western seven-pair Jade hand using Green Dragons and the green Bamboo tiles allowed by these rules.
entries.whatItMeans: The hand is entirely pair-based and uses the Jade/green tile theme rather than normal melds.
entries.whySpecial: It combines the seven-pair structure with a tight green-tile composition.

evidenceBindings.locator: §3 Pairs/Winds inventory — All Pair Jade pp.23,32,52

entries.summary: Pairs of all four Winds plus two Dragon Pungs/Kongs.
entries.whatItIs: Make a pair of each Wind, then two Dragon Pungs or Kongs.
entries.whatItMeans: The Winds are paired rather than melded; the Dragon component provides the two Pungs/Kongs.
entries.whySpecial: All four Winds are pairs, while the Dragons make the two sets.

evidenceBindings.locator: §3 Pairs/Winds inventory — Windy Dragons pp.25,46

entries.summary: Chinese Odds and Odds & Evens both use odd or even tile numbers, but the hands are built differently.
entries.whatItIs: Chinese Odds uses odd-number Pungs or Kongs in one suit. Odds & Evens uses odd ranks in two suits and even ranks in the third.
entries.whatItMeans: Chinese Odds is a usual grouped hand in one suit. Odds & Evens spreads odd ranks across two suits and even ranks across the third.
entries.whySpecial: The tile numbers themselves are part of the rule.

variants.definition: Four Pungs/Kongs and a pair of odd ranks in one suit.

variants.label: Odds & Evens

evidenceBindings.locator: §3 Dragons/honours/suit inventory — Chinese Odds p.49; Odds & Evens not illustrated

entries.summary: Four Chows across all three suits in a 1/2/1 suit distribution, plus a pair.
entries.whatItIs: Make four Chows across all three suits, plus a pair. One suit must supply two of the four Chows.
entries.whatItMeans: All three suits must be represented, but the four Chow slots cannot be distributed evenly; one suit supplies two of them.
entries.whySpecial: The four Chows use one suit twice and the other suits once each.

evidenceBindings.locator: §3 Dragons/honours/suit inventory — Robin not illustrated

entries.summary: Matching non-terminal Pungs/Kongs in each suit, plus an honour Pung/Kong and pair.
entries.whatItIs: Choose one non-terminal number and make that Pung or Kong in all three suits. Add an honour Pung or Kong and a pair.
entries.whatItMeans: The three suited melds are parallel versions of one another, differing only by suit; an honour meld and pair complete the hand.
entries.whySpecial: The same number appears as a set in every suit.

evidenceBindings.locator: §3 Dragons/honours/suit inventory — Numbers in Parallel p.43

facetDefinitionAdditions.rank-parity: Odd/even suited-rank membership is a defining qualification fact.
facetDefinitionAdditions.parallel-ranks: The same suited rank is deliberately repeated across multiple suits as corresponding groups.
